hypothesis.text: Batch repair state maintenance in `destroy_repair.py`: let `_insert_existing` and `_insert_new_route` update only the affected route/list during an insertion sequence, then perform one `remove_empty_routes()`/`rebuild_index()` after greedy or regret repair has restored every pending customer. The existing insertion ranking remains exact because `_best_insertions` consults current per-route `load` and `cost`, both maintained by `_Route.insert`, and `_new_route_cost` is independent of solution-wide indexes; the scheduler already normalizes the repaired candidate before feasibility and objective checks. Thus the same RNG-driven removal and insertion decisions generate the same fully repaired route state, while removing repeated global recalculation and index construction. This should reduce ALNS-core time per repaired customer and permit more destroy/repair-plus-VNS trajectories under the fixed deadline, yielding lower final total_distance among equal-fleet feasible solutions. Commit the final rebuild unconditionally on normal repair completion so unique coverage, capacity validation, implicit-depot routes, route-limit rejection, and the external solve interface retain their current semantics.
hypothesis.target_weakness: During every greedy or regret repair, each individual insertion calls `solution.rebuild_index()`, which recalculates every route and rebuilds both customer maps even though repair scoring reads only route loads, route costs, and `solution.routes`. With up to 200 removed customers, this repeatedly performs whole-solution work inside the most frequently executed ALNS core path; the champion's budget-exhausting search therefore spends avoidable time before the already dominant VNS phase can be reached.
hypothesis.expected_effect: Lower repair overhead and higher completed ALNS iteration throughput without changing the repaired route state for a fixed operator/RNG trajectory; preserve fleet_violation and structural feasibility, then seek lower paired final total_distance.

hypothesis.text: Replace `_or_opt`'s per-trial route-list construction and `_route_distance` calls with an exact constant-time directed delta computed from the affected boundary arcs and the moved segment's precomputed forward/reverse internal-edge cost. For each source segment, compute its removal delta once from its predecessor/successor boundaries; for each feasible destination position and orientation, add the exact insertion delta using the destination predecessor/successor and the oriented segment endpoints/internal cost. Retain the existing enumeration order, best-gain selection, strict `_EPS` acceptance condition, capacity test, deadline-reserve polling, and the current route reconstruction/recalculation/index rebuild only when committing the selected move. Thus the same move is selected for every fully scanned state—even if distances are asymmetric—while avoiding repeated O(route-length) scoring in three VNS neighborhoods. This should reduce `vns_embedded` time per attempted relocation, increase completed ALNS iterations within the same budget, and lower final total_distance among solutions with unchanged fleet_violation. Capacity, unique customer coverage, implicit-depot route representation, route-limit checks, and the public solve contract remain unchanged.
hypothesis.target_weakness: The embedded VNS consumes roughly 80% of champion runtime, and `_or_opt` repeatedly materializes a full destination trial route and recomputes its depot-to-depot distance for every candidate insertion position and segment orientation. This makes each length-1/2/3 cross-route relocation scan unnecessarily linear in route length, limiting the number of VNS and ALNS trajectories completed under the fixed deadline.
hypothesis.expected_effect: Lower VNS scoring cost and higher fixed-budget ALNS/VNS throughput without changing fully evaluated Or-opt route-state decisions; first verify no structural-feasibility or fleet-violation regression, then assess paired final total_distance.
